avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducer reduces bosutinib plasma concentrations and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative supplements with provider approval

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit extract/seed
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor increases bosutinib bioavailability and toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue supplement; allow 72+ hours washout before bosutinib initiation

avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inducer may reduce bosutinib therapeutic levels
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid use; discuss alternatives with healthcare provider

caution_supplements.name: Milk thistle
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition may modestly increase bosutinib levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased toxicity (diarrhea, GI effects); dosage adjustment may be considered

caution_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential mild CYP3A4 induction at very high doses
caution_supplements.action: Use culinary amounts without concern; limit supplemental doses

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/pomelo/Seville orange
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition increases bosutinib exposure and adverse effects
avoid_foods.action: Completely eliminate from diet; switch to other citrus fruits (oranges, lemons, limes acceptable)

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase bosutinib absorption; food effect dependent on formulation
caution_foods.action: Take consistently with or without food; maintain routine; notify provider of significant dietary changes

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (high intake)
caution_foods.mechanism: Potential mild CYP3A4 induction with very high chronic consumption
caution_foods.action: Normal dietary amounts acceptable; avoid excessive supplemental concentrated forms

monitoring_notes: Bosutinib is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4; significant drug-food interactions are possible with CYP3A4 modulators and P-glycoprotein inhibitors. Monitor for GI toxicity (diarrhea is most common adverse effect), myelosuppression, and signs of reduced efficacy when supplements or dietary patterns change.
